integrity: An exact Boolean minimum-ball projection lemma supplies the unique center and radius. Matroid rank inequalities characterize feasibility of the uniform projection in two rank regimes, giving both sharp equality classes. The quantitative deficit follows from the Pythagorean projection inequality and Cauchy--Schwarz, and a five-element direct-sum example attains its constant. Contact sets follow from the exposed projection face; numerical checks are corroborative, not an all-matroid proof.
scientific_limitations: Standard Euclidean indicator-vector embedding; finite loopless matroids with at least two elements. The universal projection formula is exact but is an optimization characterization rather than a closed coordinate expression for all matroids. The rank-defect gap is a one-sided inequality. The classical uniform-density and matroid-partition equivalences are explicitly credited.
title: Sharp minimum-sphere bounds for matroid independence polytopes distinguish uniform density from arboricity two
